E2-A.why: A minimal, concrete diff with switchable fail-safe defaults, a log-req.ip check that settles the proxy question, honest unrun/recalled-API flags, and untouched issues listed separately.

E2-B.why: Thorough findings and a sensible log-only rollout, but it grows the scope (app factory, allowlist, extra limiters), leaves recalled library options unmarked, and blocks implementation on the deployment answer.

E2-C.why: It names the decisive risk up front and ships a small diff with an enforce switch for log-only rollout, though its test is thin and it doesn't mark which specifics were recalled.

E3-A.why: A solid diagnose-then-make-idempotent plan with a useful symptom-to-cause table and correct ordering, though it misses the other reading of 'last Tuesday' and some defaults (no external consumers) are not fail-safe.

E3-B.why: It gives good containment options that keep data flowing safely, concrete queries flagged as placeholders, and a clear warning not to delete before diagnosing, but it never turns the relative date into a real one.

E3-C.why: It resolves the date with an alternative reading, defines the cause as a reproduction with the change present and reverted, gates the destructive cleanup with sign-off and count checks, and states what would change the plan.

E5-A.why: A sound CDC plan with a staged cutover, a 30-second abort rule and reverse replication; it correctly says the difficulty is the cross-table coupling, not the row count, but gives that untangling no phase of its own.

E5-B.why: Detailed and practical, with numeric exit criteria and good dialect and collation traps, but it has no abort rule during the cutover and states recalled tool settings without hedging.

E5-C.why: It sizes the real work (decoupling joins, FKs and transactions) as its own phase and adds a measurable go/no-go list, a hold timeout and replacements for lost FK integrity, despite a small inconsistency in its question-1 default.

E8-A.why: It names the three shaping decisions, with ID collision as the hardest, ships tenant-aware code before any data moves, and supports dual-mode routing with clear defaults and branches; its replacements for lost per-database capabilities are only briefly listed.

E8-B.why: Strong technical detail (RLS with SET LOCAL, a reverse tool, shard routing), but it brushes past cheaper alternatives, gives no explicit stop criteria for the waves, and doesn't mark recalled or unseen facts.

E8-C.why: It offers the cheaper schema-per-tenant path up front, then gives a complete plan with explicit wave stop criteria and a 'what you lose and what replaces it' table, ending with which answers matter most.
